answer: In an agent economy trading quartz, each seller must lock a bond in a cipher-protected escrow account before accepting work. A fixed dispute window lets buyers submit verifiable evidence of non-delivery, triggering forfeiture under the escrow rules. This makes the market a haven for accountable trade: creating extra identities grants no free capacity, since each active seller needs a separate bond. An attacker must tie up capital for every alias and risks losing it when cheating is proved.
